### UI Response Consumption And Request Shape

- `API-0001` returns six envelope fields. `ReviewsArticlesTableContainer`
  consumes only `data` and `nextCursor`; `totalCount`, `page`, `limit`, and
  `totalPages` are ignored and a later `API-0002` result drives both displayed
  total and total pages.
- The count query consumes `totalCount` and `totalPages` but never rejects or
  renders the optional route `error`, so every caught server failure becomes a
  displayed zero. Its five-minute stale time is independent of the list query,
  which declares no stale time.
- The filter query returns only `response.filters` to the component. It uses
  `promptId`, `promptName`, `filterType`, enum `answeredOriginalValues`, and
  numeric `bins.{label,min,max}`/`specialValues`; it discards top-level
  `diagnostics`, `facets`, `filterOptions`, and `searchScope`.
- The LLM table consumes list-row `id`, `articleTitle`, `articleCreatedAt`,
  `articleUpdatedAt`, `articleId`, `arxivId`, `biorxivId`, `medrxivId`, `doi`,
  `pubmedId`, `journalTitle`, `url`, `originalData`, `sourceMetadata`,
  `fullTextPDF`, `fullTextFetchedAt`, `fullTextConversionStatus`,
  `judgments[].{promptId,answeredOriginal,answeredOriginalAsArray}`,
  `judgedPromptIds`, and `isFullyJudged`. It ignores returned
  `canonicalArticleId`, `selectedImportRouteId`, and judgment
  `id`, `createdAt`, article-copy fields, `modelId`, `explanation`, and
  `quotes`.
- `loadedPages` concatenates pages `1..currentPage`, so “Load more” grows the
  rendered table. Missing cursor state on a page above one resets to page one.
  Top and bottom `ReviewsPaginationControls` instances duplicate the same
  controls and each creates a `['projects-without-jobs']` observer plus bulk
  mutations; whether one network request is shared is runtime-unknown.
- `ReviewsProjectWarnings` and `ReviewsArticlesTableContainer` each create the
  same `['project-reviews-warnings', projectId]` observer. The latter admits
  list/count reads only when `indexing.serving.readable === true`. Same-key
  TanStack source composition is not a network-deduplication observation.
- URL state covers `from`, `to`, duplicate/conflict flags, `page`, `limit`,
  `search`, `llmStatus`, and dynamic `pf_<promptId>` values. LLM status defaults
  to `complete`; typed title text affects no query until form submission copies
  it to `appliedSearchTitle`.

All eight `UIR-####` rows are source-applicable to both normal browser and
desktop renderer flows. That applicability follows shared route/client code and
desktop origin/fetch bridging; neither runtime request counts nor semantic
parity were observed. `BLK-0068` and `BLK-0069` preserve those limits.

## US-017 Human Review API And UI Surface Inventory

US-017 is a source-only inventory of the Human review list/filter routes and
their UI consumers. Actual `ProjectsRoutes.ts` composition and the public route
inventory prove both mounts; the read-contract route inventory is retained as
a separate mapping source. Current production directly calls only the Human
row, Human judgment, Human facet and Human option contracts. Rows-by-set,
named count and standalone search contracts are mapped only, while posting and
title-search tables are embedded in row/direct-count SQL.

The SQL counts below are successful-first-attempt logical `queryJson(...)`
statement counts under local DuckDB ownership, not runtime observations,
network requests, optimizer work or physical measurements. Define
`C = ceil(R / max(1, min(100, floor(10000 / P))))` for `R` returned page rows
and maximum positive enabled-prompt count `P`; the service substitutes `P =
128` when no positive count exists. Define `K = 1` on a cold cached
`information_schema.columns` lookup for `app.project`, otherwise `K = 0`.
Last-known-good selection adds two manifest statements. Date and reader data
statements allow four underlying attempts with 100, 250 and 500 ms delays. The
dynamic count layers the same helper around that retrying database and can
therefore issue four outer groups of four attempts (16 underlying attempts) if
the matching transient error persists. Retry attempts are not included in the
successful-path formulas. No live DuckDB, server, browser, desktop shell or
benchmark was opened.

### Human Prompt, Status, Mode, Freshness, And Retry Semantics

| Concern | Source-observed contract | Evidence IDs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Candidate status | The route supplies no status input and always filters candidate/direct-count SQL to `human_status_key = 'answered'`. In summary config this means at least one answered summary contribution; in prompt config it means every enabled prompt is answered. Zero enabled prompts yields null rather than answered. | `EVD-0166`, `EVD-0167` |
| Null summary answer | A Covidence-imported summary conflict can project as answered with a null answer. The route still includes the article, finds its summary judgment when present, sets mode to summary, emits `humanSummaryAnswer:null`, and always emits `isFullyJudged:true`. | `EVD-0166`, `EVD-0167` |
| Human mode authority | The filter route reads persisted project config. The list instead infers each row's mode from hydrated `promptId:"summary"`, then takes the first row's mode for the envelope and defaults an empty page to prompt. The route shell separately reads access mode only to show/hide the Human Assessment link. No source declares these three observations equivalent. | `EVD-0164`, `EVD-0166`, `EVD-0168`, `EVD-0170` |
| Prompt filters and hydration | Body prompt values become reader `promptAnswer` values and direct-count posting values `human:promptAnswer:<promptId>:<answer>`. After candidate selection, Human judgment hydration deliberately passes empty filters and returns every bounded payload row for the selected articles. | `EVD-0166`, `EVD-0169` |
| Filter construction | Summary config emits one enum filter with prompt ID `summary`, even when options are empty. Prompt config emits one filter per enabled prompt and can produce enum or numeric bins/special values. The Human UI statically treats all filters as enum and uses only `answeredOriginalValues`. | `EVD-0168`, `EVD-0170` |
| Freshness and failure | List/filter readers select active or retired LKG and pass `allowStale:true`. Human list date/reader data reads retry the named transient error at most four underlying attempts; dynamic count layers the helper around the already-retrying database and permits up to 16 underlying attempts. Config, manifest and diagnostics reads are outside the injected wrapper, and Human filters do not use it. | `EVD-0166`, `EVD-0168`, `EVD-0169` |

error. The direct count wraps that retrying database in the same helper and can
therefore issue four outer groups of four attempts, or 16 underlying attempts,
when the error persists. Retry attempts are excluded from the successful-path
formulas. No live DuckDB, server, browser, desktop shell, or benchmark was
opened.

### Both Membership, Filter, Conflict, And Composition Semantics

| Concern | Source-observed contract | Evidence IDs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Candidate membership | Both does not intersect separately fetched LLM and Human lists. Its fixed route filter LLM `complete` maps to persisted `llm_status_key='answered'`; the candidate also requires `list_mode_key='both'` and `human_status_key='answered'`. Persisted LLM answered means every enabled prompt is answered, while zero enabled prompts yields null; Human answered is summary- or prompt-mode dependent. | `EVD-0177`-`EVD-0179` |
| Count authority | Fixed statuses make `hasDynamicFilters` true even with no user filters, so the list always executes a direct distinct count and never `review.both.count`. Count repeats candidate posting/search/status work after both hydration streams and bypasses reader admission/shape checks; its layered retry permits up to 16 underlying attempts. | `EVD-0176`, `EVD-0177`, `EVD-0179` |
| Prompt filters | The shared filter UI returns review-mode LLM prompt-answer values. Both list values become posting keys `review:promptAnswer:<promptId>:<answer>` and filter candidate LLM answers; they do not filter Human answers. Selected prompt values are absent from the filter query key/body itself. | `EVD-0177`, `EVD-0180`, `EVD-0181` |
| Hydration and Human mode | After candidate selection, LLM and Human payloads are read concurrently in separate bounded article-set calls with empty filters. LLM placeholders are dropped. A Human `promptId='summary'` row selects summary mode; otherwise the row is prompt mode and non-null Human answers are grouped by prompt. | `EVD-0177`, `EVD-0179` |
| Summary composition | `llmSummaryAnswer` normalizes scalar LLM answers and resolves any `no` before any `maybe`, otherwise `yes`; no recognized scalar yields null. Summary-mode Human accepts only `yes`, `no`, or `maybe`. This response-time composition is distinct from persisted candidate statuses and the conflict summary. | `EVD-0177`, `EVD-0178` |
| Three conflict meanings | Request/UI `hasStudyDecisionConflict` filters the selected-import/Covidence `conflict_flag`. `review.both.conflictByPrompt` instead counts prompt-matched, non-null scalar LLM/Human answers that are exactly distinct and is not read by the Both page. The table independently computes normalized match/mixed/mismatch tones from hydrated answers; summary `maybe` disagreements become mixed. | `EVD-0178`, `EVD-0182` |
| Freshness and failure | Route readers select active or retired LKG and pass `allowStale:true`; missing/candidate-only state rejects with no raw fallback. Date/reader data uses the four-attempt wrapper, direct count composes it to 16 attempts, and shared filters silently turn rejected readers into empty arrays. | `EVD-0177`, `EVD-0179`, `EVD-0180` |

### Both UI Response Consumption And Request Shape

- Both URL state covers `from`, `to`, duplicate/import-conflict flags, `page`,
  `limit`, submitted `search`, and dynamic `pf_<promptId>` values. It does not
  enable or send `llmStatus`, Human status, or Human mode. Typed search affects
  no request until submit.
- The list query key is `['project-articles-both-reviews', projectId,
  duplicates, conflicts, promptFilters, page, cursor-or-null, limit, validFrom,
  validTo, appliedSearch-or-null]`. It consumes `data`, `totalCount`,
  `totalPages`, and `nextCursor`, rejects a truthy optional `error`, and ignores
  envelope `page` and `limit`. The count is embedded and snapshot-coincident;
  no separate count query or five-minute count cache exists.
- `ReviewsFilterControls` reuses the LLM-page key
  `['project-articles-reviews-filters', ...]` and `API-0006`. It consumes
  `filters[].{promptId,promptName,filterType,answeredOriginalValues,bins,
  specialValues}` and ignores diagnostics, facets, filter options, and search
  scope. Neither the key nor request includes current prompt selections or a
  Both mode marker, and the request is not warning-gated.
- The shared table consumes row `id`, title/timestamps, article/external IDs,
  URL/source/original/journal metadata, PDF fields,
  `judgments[].{promptId,answeredOriginal,answeredOriginalAsArray}`, judgment
  count, `humanJudgmentMode`, `humanAnswersByPrompt`, `humanSummaryAnswer`, and
  `llmSummaryAnswer`. It ignores returned `canonicalArticleId`,
  `selectedImportRouteId`, and judgment ID, creation/article/model/explanation/
  quote fields. Prompt mode renders only the first three LLM judgments and
  indexes matching Human answers; other prompt-map entries are not displayed.
- The table asks for `judgedPromptIds` and `isFullyJudged`, but `API-0004` does
  not return them, so its status column renders an em dash even though the page
  copy claims every row has complete LLM and Human judgments. Summary mode uses
  the two response-time summary fields; prompt mode computes tones per hydrated
  prompt. Neither is the import-conflict flag or named conflict count.
- `loadedPages` concatenates pages `1..currentPage`; missing cursor state above
  page one resets to page one. Both top and bottom pagination controls consume
  the embedded total/cursor, receive the accumulated row IDs, construct a
  `['projects-without-jobs']` observer, and own Both PDF/add mutations and
  select-all filter bodies.
- `ReviewsProjectWarnings` in the route and in the Both table container each
  construct the same five-second `['project-reviews-warnings',projectId]`
  observer. Only the list is gated on `indexing.serving.readable === true`.
  Same-key source and duplicated controls do not prove one network request.

All seven Both `UIR-####` rows are source-applicable to normal browser and
desktop renderer flows through the shared route, Eden client, and desktop
origin/fetch bridge. Neither flow was executed. `BLK-0076` and `BLK-0077`
preserve consumed/ignored-field, repeated-request, comparison, and parity
limits.

## US-019 Unassessed And Queue API And UI Surface Inventory

US-019 is a source-only inventory of the normal Unassessed review page, the
Human-assessment initialization route, the judgment-job Unassessed count and
preview routes, and the worker that consumes Unassessed prompt pairs. Actual
plugin composition plus the public route-surface inventory proves the four
HTTP mounts. The read-contract inventory is retained as a separate mapping:
the normal page directly calls `review.unassessed.rows` and conditionally
`review.unassessed.count`; Human initialization directly calls
`review.queue.unassessed` and `review.unassessed.rowsByArticleSet` only when it
does not resume an existing pending assessment. The job count, preview, and
worker do not call `readReviewServingRows`; each embeds queue-table SQL with
different scope, ordering, cursor, and result units.

The SQL counts below are successful-first-attempt logical `queryJson(...)`
statement counts under local DuckDB ownership, not runtime observations,
network requests, optimizer work, or physical measurements. An owner-HTTP
project-access read can replace one local access statement. A successful
`readReviewServingRows` call contributes diagnostics, manifest, and data
statements. Last-known-good selection adds a manifest read where supported;
job consumers require active state and do not use LKG. Retry attempts and
transaction-control statements are excluded. No live DuckDB was opened, and
no server, worker, browser, desktop shell, repository migration/projector
command, or benchmark was run. Focused tests may create disposable synthetic
fixtures.

### Queue Kinds, Eligibility, Counts, Priority, And Consumers

| Concern | Source-observed contract | Evidence IDs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unassessed` queue rows | One row per eligible article/prompt/review-config/snapshot. Project prompt and prompt record must be enabled/not archived. The latest current-model/four-content-flag LLM judgment is ineligible when answered; selected/scope tombstones also remove the row. Priority is 0 with no judgment timestamp and 1 for an existing unanswered judgment; activity uses judgment creation or scope activity. | `EVD-0190` |
| `human-unreviewed` queue rows | Prompt mode uses eligible project prompts; summary mode uses synthetic prompt ID `summary`. Nonblank Human answers tombstone rows; summary-mode Covidence import also tombstones even with an empty answer. Priority is 0 without a Human update and 1 with one; activity uses the update or scope activity. Human init nevertheless rejects summary projects. | `EVD-0190`, `EVD-0191` |
| Identity and mutability | Queue identity serializes prompt ID, queue kind, and review-config hash, while the physical row also keys project/config/snapshot/article/prompt/kind. This source identity and a successful projection do not establish deployed uniqueness, immutability, retention, or physical cardinality. | `EVD-0190` |
| Four count units | The named normal-page count sums queue prompt-pair contributions. The filtered normal-page count and job count use distinct articles under different scopes. Preview returns only up to 100 grouped articles, while worker intake returns prompt pairs. These values are not interchangeable. | `EVD-0188`, `EVD-0190`, `EVD-0192` |
| Four orderings | Normal page orders candidate article activity; registered queue orders priority/activity/article/prompt/identity; job preview groups by article and orders max priority/activity; worker orders prompt pairs by priority, millisecond-truncated activity, article, and prompt. Only the latter uses a cursor, and it omits queue identity. | `EVD-0187`-`EVD-0189`, `EVD-0192` |
| Human initialization | Existing unanswered `app.judgment_human` work bypasses queue/config/snapshot/current-scope selection. New work reads one Human queue pair, then separately reads the article without rechecking queue membership, and synchronizes pending judgments against all linked project prompts rather than the projector's enabled/nonarchived prompt set. | `EVD-0191` |
| Judgment-job consumers | Count/preview/worker require current config and an active manifest, join current enabled prompts, and reapply date plus configured-route-or-curated scope. Count/preview snapshot current project values through route-context reads; the worker joins current project/scope values inside its direct queue query. None invokes `API-0047`, and the worker cursor/order differs from it. | `EVD-0192` |
| Freshness and failure | Normal list/Human new-work can use retired LKG with `allowStale`; job consumers are active-only. Human queue rejection and empty both become a 404 empty state. Job route cache admission is driven by legacy project-mart freshness, separate from the review-serving manifest used by its direct read. | `EVD-0188`, `EVD-0191`, `EVD-0192` |

### Unassessed, Human-Init, And Job UI Consumption

- The Unassessed route shell uses project access/detail plus URL state for
  dates, duplicate/import-conflict flags, page, limit, and submit-only search.
  `useUrlFilters` can retain `pf_<promptId>` URL values, but the shell supplies
  empty/no-op prompt state and `hidePromptSelectors:true`; the filter-summary
  query is disabled and no prompt applicability value reaches `API-0005`.
- Its list key is `['project-articles-unassessed',projectId,duplicates,
  conflicts,page,cursor-or-null,limit,validFrom,validTo,
  appliedSearch-or-null]`. It has no explicit polling and disables focus
  refetch. The list is enabled only when the five-second warning observer says
  serving is readable; the route and container construct the same warning key.
- The container consumes `data`, `totalCount`, `totalPages`, and `nextCursor`,
  ignores envelope `page`/`limit`, accumulates pages `1..current`, and resets to
  page one when a cursor is missing. Its “has filters” copy checks only date and
  search, not duplicate/conflict flags. Both pagination controls create the
  shared jobs observer and Unassessed PDF/add mutations using accumulated IDs.
- The shared table consumes identifiers/title/timestamps/URL, journal,
  original/source metadata, PDF fields, and the returned empty judgment/status
  fields. It ignores `canonicalArticleId` and `selectedImportRouteId`; an empty
  judgment array plus `isFullyJudged:false` renders the shared partial-status
  presentation rather than queue priority or missing-prompt detail.
- Human assessment uses `['human-assessment-init',projectId]`, `staleTime:0`,
  no explicit interval, and default focus behavior. It consumes project name,
  article title/summary, prompt ID/text/type, and pending judgment ID/prompt ID;
  it ignores project/article IDs and prompt heading/order. Prompt type selects
  string versus enum inputs. Submit success refetches the exact init key.
- Job detail uses `['judgments-job-unassessed-count',jobId]`, focus refetch,
  and status-derived polling: 10 seconds while storage drains, 30 seconds for
  active nonterminal job states, and none for terminal states. It keeps only
  count and ignores freshness/status. The preview uses
  `['judgments-job-unassessed-articles',jobId]`, fixed 30-second polling and
  manual retry; its service discards error/freshness and its table displays the
  returned array length plus article ID/title/authors/date/link fields.
- All ten US-019 `UIR-####` rows are source-applicable to normal browser and
  desktop renderer flows through shared generated Solid routes, Eden client,
  origin injection, and the desktop fetch bridge. Neither runtime was executed;
  polling counts, same-key deduplication, cache behavior, errors, rendering,
  runtime assets, and semantic parity remain `BLK-0081` and `BLK-0082`.

## US-020 Detail, Prompt, Full-Text, And Admin Surface Inventory

US-020 is a source-only inventory of detail-only and hydration behavior. Actual
plugin composition and the public route-surface inventory prove the mounted
project review detail, prompt preview, global article detail, and article
admin-info routes. Registry membership remains separate evidence: the project
detail route invokes four registered detail contracts but also reads mutable
`app` tables; the prompt-preview registry maps `review.detail.payload`, while
the mounted route actually invokes `review.detail.row`; global article detail
and admin-info use direct `app` reads and have no review-serving contract.

The bounds below are source contracts, not physical observations. A successful
active `readReviewServingRows` call contributes diagnostics, manifest, and data
statements. Project detail recursively reads 512-row LLM and Human pages, so
the per-call caps do not bound the route aggregate. Initial article detail and
payload reads require active state, while later judgment reads explicitly
allow retired last-known-good state; none of the separate calls is pinned to a
single returned snapshot ID. Direct full-text, residual judgment, Covidence,
project-name, model, and admin reads use current mutable `app` state. No live
DuckDB was opened and no server, browser, desktop shell, worker, projector,
repository migration, benchmark, or production-data command ran. Focused
database tests used only disposable synthetic temporary fixtures.

### Candidate, Hydration, And Freshness Boundaries

| Surface | Candidate or keyed selection | Post-selection hydration | Consumed/ignored boundary | Snapshot/freshness consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project review detail | `API-0051` and `API-0052` independently key one article; detail SQL also joins payload before `LIMIT 1`. | Mutable full text and uncapped residual judgments, Covidence, recursive `API-0053`, optional project names, then recursive `API-0054`. Serving payload gaps may be filled from residual judgments after an accepted detail page. | UI uses article/full text, current and historical judgments, Human answers/assessments, summaries, project names, and Covidence; top-level `prompts` and `martFreshness` are ignored. | Initial active candidate can be composed with later active or LKG judgment pages and current app rows; no response snapshot/freshness ID is returned. |
| Prompt preview | `API-0055` chooses the earliest payload row under current config; payload columns are part of the ordered candidate read. | Separate `API-0051`, mutable model metadata, optional full text, then prompt construction/truncation. | UI uses status/reason/article ID/title/combined preview and ignores diagnostics plus separate system/user prompts. | Both readers require active state but can observe different promotions; mutable config/model/full text is not frozen with either reader. |
| Global article/full text | Direct keyed `app.article` lookup, not a review candidate and not project-scoped. | All matching judgment history with no cap, then optional snapshot-project names. Both tabs receive full text even when only the summary tab is open. | UI uses article identity/title/authors/summary, URL/source inputs, full text/HTML/PDF, content hash, history, and project names; many conversion/provenance/timestamp fields are ignored. | Entire response is current mutable state with only five-minute client caching; no serving snapshot or freshness envelope exists. |
| Article admin support | Direct keyed projection of eight `app.article` fields. | No server hydration; it is a client-side waterfall beside each detail query. Mutations and pending polling cause later detail/admin invalidations. | UI ignores conversion attempts but renders timestamps/PDF/source/status/error and conditionally character count. | Thirty-second cache and three-second invalidation are client behavior, not a persisted lease, freshness proof, or snapshot fence. |

### Detail, Full-Text, Prompt, And Admin UI Consumption

- The project summary and full-text tabs independently declare the same
  `['article-review-details',projectId,articleId]` query and five-minute stale
  time. TanStack source sharing makes deduplication possible, but no runtime
  observation proves request count or cache reuse across navigation.
- Available project detail consumes article/title/summary/identifier/URL,
  full-text/HTML/PDF, judgment/prompt/model/answer/explanation/quote/assessment,
  Human mode/answers/summaries, cross-project names, and Covidence fields.
  `prompts` and `martFreshness` are ignored; the unavailable branch consumes
  status/reason but not the full diagnostic/empty-field envelope.
- Both global tabs independently declare `['article-details',articleId]` and
  receive the same broad response. The summary route therefore receives full
  text, raw/source metadata, assets, conversion metadata, and complete history
  even when those fields are not rendered. The full-text tab adds no narrower
  server request.
- `ArticleAdminSection` adds `['article-admin-info',articleId]` on all four
  tabs. It ignores conversion attempts, polls by invalidation only while status
  is pending, and owns three mutations whose success invalidates both global
  and project detail keys. This is a separate freshness contract, not evidence
  that the base detail response is current.
- Prompt preview is mounted only after an eligible prompt card is toggled. It
  uses `['project',projectId,'prompt-preview',promptId]`, consumes the combined
  preview text and availability copy, and ignores separate prompts/diagnostics.
  The client reason type omits `serving_detail_unavailable` and manifest
  freshness values returned by the server; those values fall into generic copy.
- All seven new `UIR-####` rows are source-applicable to browser and desktop
  renderer flows through shared generated routes, Eden, origin injection, and
  the desktop fetch bridge. No browser/desktop route execution, response size,
  request/poll count, mutation, asset load, or semantic-parity capture ran.

## US-021 Warning, Health, Readiness, And Progress Surface Inventory

US-021 is a source-only inventory of diagnostic, readiness, and progress
contracts. Actual plugin composition and the public route inventory prove that
project warnings, runtime readiness, PDF-job status, and add-articles-job status
are mounted. The health handler is source-defined but absent from
`ProjectsRoutes.ts` and the mounted public inventory even though the review
read-contract inventory and parity coverage still declare it mounted. Its route
row therefore remains blocked rather than being promoted from registry evidence.

Polling intervals below are client source declarations, not observed network
frequency. The warning surface has two same-key observers on each of four review
pages and a five-second interval, but source sharing does not prove one network
request. More importantly, the warning POST is not a pure diagnostic read: when
serving is unusable and progress is stale, it may boost or enqueue a V4 rebuild
request while suppressing mutation errors. Runtime readiness always returns an
HTTP-success envelope and places semantic availability in `data.ready`; the
shared renderer checks that field, while desktop startup accepts `response.ok`
without parsing it. Add-article jobs poll durable status every two seconds until
a recognized terminal value. PDF controls retain only the created job ID and
never call the mounted PDF status route.

No live DuckDB was opened. No server, browser, desktop shell, worker, projector,
repository migration, repair command, benchmark, or production-data command
ran. The focused warning-route test created only its disposable synthetic
temporary database.

## US-022 Inventory Search, Selection, And Add-To-Project Surfaces

US-022 is a source-only inventory. It separates the search box that submits
all-token title-prefix predicates to the four review list families from the
standalone token-prefix read contract and from the persisted async-substring
job path. The browser UI has no substring caller. The mounted add-by-filter
route always creates `review.bulk.selection` with `tokenPrefix` or `none`,
while the read-contract route inventory maps that route only to
`review.bulk.substringSelection`; the worker explicitly rejects that substring
kind because no completed search result is attached.

Selection is also split into separate contracts. The controls accumulate every
loaded page, call that set the current-page rows, and can either send those IDs
or replace them with mutable select-all criteria. The displayed total is not a
frozen membership manifest: LLM uses a separate five-minute count, Human and
Both use list-envelope counts, and Unassessed can count prompt pairs rather
than distinct articles. Filter jobs store no snapshot ID or pin and resolve the
current active serving manifest on each worker batch. Explicit-ID jobs are
bounded at 5,000 IDs and 1,000,000 stable-JSON bytes, but the UI performs no
matching preflight. Worker progress counts selected batch rows, while the
writer independently deduplicates IDs, rejects missing articles, ignores
existing project membership, and returns insertion counts that the worker does
not consume.

All review search and add calls use TanStack Query/mutations over the shared
Eden `apiClient`. No direct renderer `fetch` call was found for these surfaces.
In a proxy-role server, owner-dependent paths are buffered and forwarded once
through the browser HTTP proxy after owner discovery; non-idempotent POSTs are
not replayed after a transport failure. Desktop injects an API origin into the
same renderer client rather than owning a distinct native selection bridge.
These are source paths, not browser/desktop runtime observations.

No live DuckDB was opened. No server, browser, desktop shell, worker,
projector, migration, repair, benchmark, or production-data command ran. No
storage disposition is made or strengthened.

## US-023 Inventory PDF, Export, And Transfer Surfaces

US-023 is a source-only inventory of generated-output and portability
consumers. It does not treat a completed selection job as a frozen export.
Filtered and project-scoped PDF jobs store latest-snapshot semantics with no
pin, and the bulk worker resolves the active serving manifest again for each
article-ID page. Explicit-ID PDF jobs avoid serving selection, but still share
the same oldest-job claim, counters, retry, and terminal-state machinery. The
PDF worker then performs a separate external-source fetch and stable-key local
file write before updating mutable article fields; `/api/runtime-asset` serves
the referenced path later. The review controls start PDF work through Eden but
never read the mounted status route, while the PDF cell exposes the generated
file through a browser/desktop runtime-asset URL.

Project CSV export also has two distinct phases. `review.export.selection`
stores ordered article-ID batches and either latest or caller-supplied pinned
snapshot metadata. The completed job does not contain the CSV rows. Download
re-resolves each source snapshot scope, then hydrates current article fields,
serving article rows, prompt details, and judgment details in 500-ID batches
before streaming CSV. The declared 10,000,000-byte payload budget is returned
as contract metadata but is not enforced across the stream. The UI creates and
polls this job with direct `fetch`, opens the completed CSV URL, and separately
uses a POST/blob/object-URL helper for prompt export.

Project transfer is a third contract family. The summary is a current-table
read outside the later package transaction. Export serializes ordered app-table
families in one DuckDB transaction, but physical asset discovery/copy and ZIP
assembly occur afterward. Small packages may be returned inline; larger work
is represented by an owner-token session with durable phase/counter progress,
24-hour expiry, startup/interval recovery, terminal cleanup, and later pruning.
Ready downloads validate session expiry and file presence and return checksum,
fingerprint, byte-length, and expiry headers, but have no persisted download
lease. The shared UI mixes direct fetch for summary/start/download with Eden
for session polling and checks only ZIP content type before saving the blob.

The renderer URL helpers apply to both browser and desktop, with desktop API
origin injection and conditional owner proxying. This establishes source
applicability, not executed caller order, request count, file integrity, save
semantics, cleanup-safe concurrency, or browser/desktop parity.

No live DuckDB was opened. No server, browser, desktop shell, worker,
projector, migration, repair, export, transfer, benchmark, or production-data
command ran. No storage disposition is made or strengthened.

## US-024 Browser LLM And Human Runtime Verification

US-024 uses only approved non-live test evidence. Fifteen isolated Bun test
processes exercised fake `queryJson` and manifest adapters plus in-process
Elysia `Request`/`Response` handling; one isolated Vitest process rendered the
warning component in its test DOM. These executions corroborate current
service, route, admission, SQL-shape, response, and warning-render branches.
They do not become production, physical, or actual-browser observations.

The browser skill requires the shared in-app browser controller, but this
session exposed neither its supported controller capability nor a discovery
call. No other browser automation surface was substituted. The checked-in
Playwright configuration was also not run: it removes and creates a synthetic
DuckDB, starts API/app servers, creates provider/model/project data, and exercises
mutations. That conflicts with this story's no-database-data boundary, and no
immutable fixture identity or complete benchmark-critical configuration was
approved. `BLK-0104` preserves the resulting browser-runtime gap.

No live DuckDB, snapshot query, server listener, app server, browser, desktop
shell, worker, projector, migration, repair, or data mutation ran. Every test
process exited before audit edits began, so the started-process cleanup set is
empty. No storage disposition is made or strengthened.

### Request, Field, Count, And Waterfall Reconciliation

| Flow | Frozen/current request and ordering contract | Executed non-live result | Browser/runtime limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LLM initial/list | Two same-key warning observers and an ungated filter GET are source-constructed. After URL initialization and `serving.readable===true`, list POST sends page/limit/cursor, valid dates, submitted trimmed search, duplicate/conflict flags, nonempty prompt values, and default/selected LLM status. Candidate order is `sort_key DESC, article_id ASC`, `limit+1`, max 500. | In-process HTTP forwarded filtered and all three status bodies unchanged. Fake-adapter service returned the selected row, one bounded judgment hydration, direct count, `nextCursor`, and exact row fields; one-chunk list used four fake data-adapter statements, excluding manifest/diagnostic adapters. Limit 500 emitted `LIMIT 501`. | No browser request order, timing, generated-client serialization, response bytes, query retry, cache, or rendered table capture. The two warning observers may deduplicate at runtime, but source construction is not proof. |
| LLM count | Count POST excludes page/cursor and is enabled only after list success and idle. It repeats the filter/search/count selection, has five-minute stale time, and performs no row/judgment hydration. | Fake-adapter count used two data-adapter statements and returned `{totalCount:1,totalPages:1}`. In-process HTTP failure returned status 200 with `{totalCount:0,totalPages:0,error}`. | UI source consumes totals and ignores `error`; no browser capture proves the list-then-count waterfall, five-minute cross-query freshness, zero display, or retry/refocus behavior. |

When readable, one list POST sends page/limit/cursor, valid dates, submitted search, duplicate/conflict flags, and nonempty Human prompt values. Candidate order is the same keyset with fixed `humanStatus=answered`; count is embedded, not a second HTTP request. | Fake-adapter service used four data-adapter statements for rows, one Human payload read, and direct distinct count; the HTTP summary fixture returned top-level/per-row summary mode and answer. ## US-026 Browser Detail And Diagnostic Runtime Verification

US-026 uses bounded non-live evidence only. Eighteen isolated Bun processes
executed fake-adapter services, in-process Elysia requests, read-contract and
SQL guards, source inventories, and two migration-backed disposable fixtures;
three isolated Vitest processes rendered detail, prompt, and warning components
in a test DOM. The two DuckDB-backed tests used unique temporary runtime roots,
closed their connections, and removed their fixtures before their processes
exited. They are synthetic test evidence, not approved physical, deployed, or
live-database observations.

The four review entry paths converge in source: LLM, Both, and Unassessed render
the generic review table, Human renders its Human table, and every article-title
link targets `/projects/$id/reviews-llm/$articleId`. This proves shared route
applicability, not a browser navigation. The browser-client script is installed,
but the mandatory in-app JavaScript controller and discovery capability are not
exposed in this session. The checked-in Playwright choices either create and
mutate synthetic database/provider/model/project state or open an existing
database, and no immutable non-mutating browser fixture, capture, or complete
benchmark-critical configuration was approved. No listener, app server,
browser, desktop shell, worker, projector, repair command, or live DuckDB was
started. `BLK-0106` preserves the actual-browser and fixture gap.

## US-028 Desktop LLM And Human Runtime Verification

US-028 uses only approved non-live evidence. Twenty-four isolated Bun test
processes exercised the current desktop configuration, single-instance lease,
hash-history selector, API-origin helpers, server-role/background/readiness
contracts, fake LLM/Human route adapters, in-process Elysia requests, and
reader/admission/manifest/SQL guards. One isolated Vitest process rendered the
shared warning component in its test DOM. A disposable source-generated probe
decoded the actual desktop preload, installed it over a synthetic window and
ElectroBun bridge, and invoked the shared Eden LLM/Human query builders. The
probe was removed immediately after it exited.

Those executions establish bounded serialization and source-path behavior;
they do not become a packaged-desktop, physical-fixture, or deployed
observation. The desktop shell was not started. Its normal startup creates the
application data/log roots, launches `src/server/index.ts` against the
app-owned DuckDB path, runs startup migration/recovery and background work, and
therefore cannot be exercised under this story's no-database-data boundary
without an approved immutable non-mutating desktop profile. The checked-in
desktop build/dev commands likewise do not supply an immutable fixture,
benchmark configuration, or desktop request/render collector.

No live DuckDB, snapshot query, migration, listener, browser, ElectroBun
window, desktop backend, worker, projector, repair, retention, or product-data
command ran. Every test/probe/lint process exited. No storage disposition is
made or strengthened. `BLK-0108` preserves the actual-desktop, hash-navigation,
restart, fixture, and collector gap.

## US-029 Desktop Both And Unassessed Runtime Verification

US-029 uses only approved non-live evidence. Thirty isolated Bun test
processes exercised desktop configuration, origin/history selection,
single-instance and restart-source guards, fake Both/Unassessed route and
projector adapters, in-process Elysia requests, queue/count contracts, Human
init and job services, and reader/admission/manifest/SQL guards. One isolated
Vitest process rendered warning states in its test DOM. A disposable
source-generated probe decoded the actual desktop preload, installed it over a
synthetic window and ElectroBun bridge, and invoked current shared Eden query
builders and callers. The probe was removed immediately after it exited.

The probe establishes serialization through the patched renderer `fetch` only.
Its warning, filter, repeated Both, repeated Unassessed, Human-init, job-count,
and job-preview calls were manually sequenced against fake responses; they do
not establish the mounted UI waterfall, TanStack scheduling, Bun-side webview
handler, loopback route execution, physical queue, count cardinality, or
rendering. Response totals `2` and `7` are synthetic assertion values, not
measurements. Passing service/projector tests remain synthetic and do not prove
deployed queue contents, physical order, or count parity.

The desktop shell was not started. Normal startup creates the application
data/log roots, launches `src/server/index.ts` against the app-owned DuckDB,
and runs migration, recovery, and background work. No approved immutable
non-mutating desktop data root, complete benchmark-critical configuration, or
ElectroBun request/render/restart collector was supplied. No live DuckDB,
snapshot query, migration, listener, browser, ElectroBun window, desktop
backend, worker, projector, repair, retention, or product-data command ran.
Every test/probe/lint process exited, no transient probe remains, and no storage
disposition is made or strengthened. `BLK-0109` preserves the native desktop,
queue/count, hash-navigation, restart, fixture, and collector gap.

## US-030 Desktop Detail And Diagnostic Runtime Verification

US-030 uses only approved non-live evidence. Twenty-six unique Bun test files
were executed twice in isolated processes: the first pass retained complete
per-file output and the second produced an exact aggregate. Three isolated
Vitest processes rendered prompt, judgment, and warning components in a test
DOM. Two tests created fully migrated synthetic DuckDB fixtures under unique
temporary runtime roots; both closed their connections and removed their roots
before exit. They are test fixtures, not live, deployed, or approved physical
desktop evidence.

A disposable source-generated probe decoded the current desktop preload,
installed it over a synthetic `views:` window and ElectroBun bridge, and called
the current Eden detail, prompt, global article, admin, warning, readiness,
add-status, and PDF-status surfaces. Its first attempt exposed a probe-only Bun
global mismatch and reached no response at the unused synthetic port; after the
probe made `window.fetch` and `globalThis.fetch` identical as they are in a
renderer, the authoritative run emitted and asserted nine messages. The probe
was removed immediately. Those fake responses establish serialization and
buffering only, not mounted UI scheduling, Bun-side forwarding, loopback route

## US-031 Desktop Search, Bulk, PDF, And Export Runtime Verification

US-031 uses only approved non-live evidence. Forty-six isolated Bun test files
ran once and then repeated in separate processes with JUnit summaries. Two
isolated Vitest files exercised transfer/export entry and inline ZIP/status/
anchor behavior in a test DOM. A disposable source-generated probe decoded the
actual desktop preload, installed it over a synthetic renderer and ElectroBun
bridge, and invoked current search query builders, Eden callers, direct-fetch
callers, URL helpers, binary responses, and prompt-download cleanup. The probe
was removed immediately after its final successful run.

The authoritative probe establishes exact renderer-side serialization and
buffered decoding only. Its 18 requests and all responses were manually ordered
against fake values. IDs such as `add-filter-1`, `pdf-filter-1`, `export-1`, and
`transfer-1`, the two search rows, progress counters, 11 ZIP bytes, and
`ready:false` are synthetic assertions, not deployed measurements. Project CSV
and PDF file links are URL anchors rather than `fetch` calls, so their exact
desktop loopback URLs were asserted without claiming a bridge message or native
download.

Per test pass, the transfer session repository and recovery files created 25
fully migrated disposable DuckDB fixtures under unique `/tmp` paths. Each test
closed its connection and removed its database, sidecars, runtime root, and
generated package/session files. Focused route tests left two 2-byte plan files,
one 8-byte upload, and two empty export directories under the test-owned
`tmp/project-transfer` root; only those timestamp-matched US-031 artifacts were
removed. No current/live DuckDB, product project, snapshot command, retained
generated output, or benchmark database was opened or changed.

The desktop shell was not started. Normal startup creates the app data/log
roots, opens and migrates `desktop/forska.duckdb`, runs transfer recovery, and
starts role-dependent background work. No approved immutable non-mutating data
root, complete benchmark-critical configuration, or ElectroBun request/render/
download/restart collector was supplied. No listener, browser, `BrowserWindow`,
desktop backend, worker heartbeat, projector, migration command, production
recovery/cleanup, or product-data process ran. Every test/probe/lint process
exited. `BLK-0111` preserves the native desktop/fixture/output gap and
`BLK-0112` preserves the source-defined executor/resume gap; no storage
disposition is made or strengthened.

## US-032 Article, Import, And Project-Scope Mutation Inventory

US-032 freezes source mutations and their first review-serving effects without
executing a production writer or opening live DuckDB. A mutation row names the
route or operator, the actual production writer, every material table or file
family it reads and writes, the delta or dirty-work boundary, lifecycle and
recovery behavior, exact tests, and stable manifest IDs. A route that appends a
delta is not recorded as directly creating dirty work: the later delta-intake
services own `DBO-0108`, and their incomplete outbox/replay/retention contract
remains `BLK-0024`/`BLK-0027`.

### US-032 Evidence Boundary

| Boundary | Recorded result |
| --- | --- |
| Source identity | Commit `8f1388e206ece2f28f49e41909e7f89778fa316f`; Ralph's pre-existing `tasks/prd.json` modification was the only worktree change before US-032. |
| Allowed evidence | Production route composition, route/service/writer SQL, runtime path builders, recovery registration, exact source tests, and isolated disposable test processes. |
| Prohibited evidence | No live/current DuckDB, snapshot profile, server, worker, migration, projector, cleanup operator, import network call, upload, desktop shell, or product-data mutation was run. No source-defined default or synthetic count is a physical observation. |
| State and disposition | New manifest rows use only the US-001 `auditStatus` vocabulary. `proofCheckState`, `recommendationActionability`, and `overallCertification` remain separate; no `DSP-####`, proof state, target shape, implementation slice, or storage disposition changed. |

### Initial Review-Serving Effect Reconciliation

- Source configuration and source archive are not review-serving mutations by
  themselves. Effective membership remains the independent union of
  `DBO-0005` article-route links and `DBO-0009` project-route membership.
- Canonical article create/update appends `DBO-0095`; import current-link
  add/rank/remove upserts/tombstones `DBO-0098` and appends `DBO-0094`.
  Neither writer directly inserts `DBO-0108`; delta intake owns that later
  transition, and the absent production outbox producer/drainer remains a
  recovery blocker.
- Project route membership emits one project-config delta. Direct project-
  article membership emits scope deltas, but removal is suppressed while an
  import route keeps the article in effective scope. Subproject and clone
  creation emit config/prompt/scope deltas for their new project.
- Archive/unarchive emits a project-config `archived` change. Delete request
  and hard cleanup emit no additional review delta or rebuild; their safety
  therefore depends on the prior archive signal and complete cleanup/serving
  exclusion contracts.
- Transfer commit is the only inventoried mutation that writes the broad
  imported project/article/prompt/judgment/Human/review set atomically with
  history and transfer dirty tokens. Its review deltas still enter the same
  later intake/reconciliation path as ordinary writers.

## US-033 Judgment And Human-Review Mutation Inventory

US-033 freezes the production writer inventory for LLM judgments, Human
judgments, prompt merge/cleanup, write overlays, and legacy review-state rows.
It treats a model answer, an active canonical judgment, a job-local completion,
an imported outbox marker, a project-scoped review delta, a dirty-work range,
and a comparison-serving invalidation as separate identities. It likewise
treats Human pending state, answered state, delete/move provenance, delta
tombstones, reviewer overlays, and projected visibility as separate contracts.
No production writer, cron, importer, projector, cleanup path, or database was
executed to create this inventory.

| Prerequisite | US-032 is complete and its `BGO-0006`-`BGO-0019` source/import/project/transfer writers remain unchanged. US-033 cross-references those rows where the same transaction also writes judgments or review state. |
| Allowed evidence | Mounted route composition; exact route/service/worker SQL; job-local SQLite declarations and path owners; cron/startup/recovery registration; literal production call closure; exact adjacent tests; isolated disposable test processes. |
| Prohibited evidence | No live/current DuckDB, server, judgment worker, import cron, projector, delta intake loop, migration, maintenance/cleanup operator, browser, desktop shell, network model request, or product-data mutation ran. Test-created DuckDB/SQLite files lived under isolated temporary roots. |
| State and disposition | New rows use only the US-001 `auditStatus` vocabulary. `proofCheckState`, `recommendationActionability`, and `overallCertification` remain independent; no `DSP-####`, proof state, target shape, implementation slice, or storage disposition changed. |

### Judgment And Review Identity Boundaries

| Contract | Persisted identity | Consequence for mutation tracing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Active LLM natural identity | `(article_id,prompt_id,model_id,use_title,use_abstract,use_fulltext,use_fulltext_no_images)` with `deleted_at IS NULL` | The current producer treats an active match as immutable. `project_id`, snapshot metadata, answer value, and chunking are not part of this lookup. |
| Physical LLM uniqueness | The same seven dimensions plus `delete_generation`; `DBO-0032` defaults generation to zero | A soft delete frees re-creation only when its writer advances the old row's generation. `deleted_at` alone does not remove the generation-zero conflict. |
| Job-local LLM completion | `DBO-0040` has AUTOINCREMENT `outbox_seq`, unique `queue_prompt_id`, and unique `judgment_id`; owner handoff `DBO-0041` is keyed by `claim_id` and validated against `DBO-0038` snapshot/claim identity | Job-local success is durable before canonical import but is not yet a canonical judgment or review delta. Queue completion, token-use closeout, and outbox evidence have separate acknowledgements. |
| Imported LLM completion | `DBO-0039` primary key `(job_id,outbox_seq)` plus canonical `DBO-0032` physical identity | Marker identity makes a committed batch replayable. An unmarked duplicate canonical identity can still receive per-project `judgment.llm.created` deltas even though no new canonical row is inserted. |
| Human prompt judgment | `DBO-0033` row ID/human key plus unique `(project_id,article_id,prompt_id)`; `project_id` is nullable and SQL nulls are distinct | Pending, answered, moved, and deleted state is project/prompt scoped. ### Initial Mutation-To-Serving Reconciliation

- Current judgment execution durably closes into job-local SQLite before it
  becomes a canonical LLM row. Only `BGO-0021` imports `DBO-0032`, appends
  project-visible deltas, and immediately intakes those ranges to `DBO-0108`.
  Ordinary route and legacy writers stop at `DBO-0095`; their later intake
  still depends on the general reconciliation path and its existing
  `BLK-0024`/`BLK-0027` gaps.
- The active LLM predicate excludes deleted rows, but physical uniqueness does
  not. Project prompt cleanup advances the deleted generation; invalid-answer
  and admin unexpected-answer paths do not. Those paths also differ in project
  fan-out, comparison invalidation, and recovery.
- Human pending rows are not review deltas. Human submit makes blank optional
  rows answered without a delta/overlay, while every Human delete path reuses
  `judgment.human.updated` or emits nothing; no Human delete change kind or
  uniform old-identity tombstone exists.
- Reviewer overlays are generated only for nonblank Human submit rows. Callable
  row/detail reads, reconcile, and expire functions are not registered in
  production, so overlay persistence is not evidence of UI application or
  terminal cleanup.
- Prompt merge collision handling, noncollision moves, project prompt cleanup,
  global prompt archive/hash/delete, and prompt-row removal after merge are
  separate transactions/contracts. Review-state `DBO-0035` remains
  transfer/cleanup-owned, not an ordinary Human-review write target.

## US-034 Project Review-Configuration Mutation Inventory

US-034 freezes the production mutation inventory for every benchmark-critical
project review-configuration surface requested by this story. Project row
identity, effective article scope, immutable prompt identity, project-prompt
membership, model/provider execution identity, review-config hashing,
execution snapshots, transfer dependency fingerprints, comparison-serving
staleness, and transfer target-state dirty tokens remain separate contracts.
No production writer, importer, projector, repair, cleanup path, or database
was executed to create this inventory.

### Review-Configuration Identity Boundaries

| Contract | Complete source-observed identity dimensions | Mutation consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Project row | `app.project.id`; values include model ID, Human mode, four content flags, two nullable date bounds, archive state, name/description | A row update is not itself a review configuration history/version. Name/description are outside benchmark config; archive/date and route fields are outside the review hash despite named config deltas. |
| Effective project article scope | Direct `(project_id,article_id)`/project-article UUID plus selected `(project_id,import_route_id)` and current article-route membership | Direct membership emits per-article append-patch deltas. Selected-route replacement emits one project config rebuild; it does not enumerate the derived article add/remove set. |
| Immutable prompt content | Prompt UUID plus normalized original/transformed text, heading, type, and MD5 `content_hash`; review prompt hash uses prompt ID, text hash, answer-schema hash, settings version, threshold version | Reusing or creating an immutable prompt is distinct from linking it to a project. Nullable/legacy hash fallback remains a separate identity rule. |
| Project-prompt membership/config | Link UUID; natural `(project_id,prompt_id)`; prompt order, enabled, archived, origin, and dynamic criteria metadata | Review hash uses active prompt ID/config hash/order. Criteria, origin, and link UUID are excluded; config field vocabulary names thresholding but not each criteria key. |
| Model row | Model UUID; natural `(provider_connection_id,remote_model_id,COALESCE(variant,''))`; display, enabled, metadata/options, version and provider disabled-model set | Review execution identity uses model ID, provider connection/kind/base, remote ID, variant, and `metadata_json.$.options`; display/enabled/version and other metadata can mutate outside the hash. |
| Provider connection | Connection UUID; provider kind, base URL, auth mode, label, enabled, max-inflight, config JSON, secret reference and external keychain value | Review hash uses connection ID/kind/base only. Execution snapshots and transfer fingerprints include broader provider state; secret lifecycle is not transactional with DuckDB. |
| Active LLM reuse | `(article_id,prompt_id,model_id,use_title,use_abstract,use_fulltext,use_fulltext_no_images)` with `deleted_at IS NULL`; physical identity also adds generation | Model/provider execution changes can invalidate review config without changing an already persisted judgment's natural identity. |
| Review config hash | Human mode; model ID; execution identity `{modelExecutionOptions,modelId,providerBaseUrl,providerConnectionId,providerKind,remoteModelId,variant}`; sorted active prompt `{promptId,promptConfigHash,promptOrder}`; four content flags | Dates, selected routes, archive, criteria, provider auth/secret/enabled/max-inflight, and model display/enabled/version are not hash dimensions. No one hash is the authority for every applicability contract. |
| Review delta | Change kind; project/prompt/field set; source partition/table/row/operation/updated time/mutation key/high-water/idempotency identity | Appending `project.reviewConfig.updated`, `prompt.config.updated`, or scope deltas does not prove intake, comparison invalidation, transfer-plan invalidation, or durable config history. |
| Selected-import and serving publication | Project ID, project-scope identity, import/source high-water and definition version form selected-import identity; serving snapshots compose project ID, review-config hash, selected-import snapshot and component watermarks | Date/route/scope mutations can alter applicability without being review-hash inputs. A later rebuild/promotion is separate from writer commit. |
| Execution snapshot | Job/queue/claim identity plus project/model/provider/prompt/article/import payload, including broader model/provider/project fields than the review hash | Existing job snapshots are immutable execution evidence; a current config delta does not rewrite or cancel them unless a writer's explicit job gate does so. |

### Configuration-To-Serving And Recovery Reconciliation

- The review hash, changed-field vocabulary, invalidation registry, active
  judgment identity, execution snapshot, and transfer fingerprint each use a
  different dimension set. Dates and selected routes affect applicability and
  trigger a full rebuild but are outside the review hash; prompt criteria and
  several provider/model fields are outside both the hash and closed field
  vocabulary.
- `project.reviewConfig.updated` begins a project-wide component rebuild,
  `prompt.config.updated` begins a prompt-scoped rebuild, and direct scope uses
  append patches. None of those rules includes comparison serving or transfer
  target-state dirty tokens.
- Comparison invalidation is writer-specific. Full project prompt edit marks it
  stale, while ordinary core/date/route/mode, model/provider, global prompt,
  clone, and transfer configuration writers do not uniformly do so.
- Transfer target-state dirty tokens advance for provider/model repository
  mutations and transfer commit/history, but not ordinary project, route,
  direct-scope, project-prompt, clone, subproject, or Covidence changes.
- Ordinary route writers generally couple row changes and `DBO-0095` append in
  one transaction, but no durable configuration version, old/new payload,
  immutable mutation manifest, optimistic compare-and-swap, or replay journal
  exists. Later review-delta intake retains the existing
  `BLK-0024`/`BLK-0027` recovery gaps.
- Clone and specialized project creation copy current source state, while
  transfer uses a frozen plan and history. Neither current-state success nor a
  transfer history row proves common source snapshot, config validation,
  comparison, dirty-token, or postcommit-settlement parity.
- Human mode is a review-hash input, not a Human-row migration. Changing it
  rebuilds review-serving components but leaves prompt/summary Human rows and
  legacy review rows under their independent writer/lifecycle contracts.

## US-035 Intake, Scope, Selected-Import, And Display Projectors

US-035 freezes the source-to-scope projection pipeline at commit
`af1909c7dd248547ab9463957abb1abc72ddbe49`. It treats source outbox recovery,
delta reconciliation, dirty-work production, rebuild admission, scheduler and
worker execution, physical project scope, selected-import state, and final
display publication as separate contracts. Source-defined callable helpers are
not promoted to operating schedulers, a completed snapshot is not treated as
immutable merely because its status says `completed`, and direct serving-table
mutation is not renamed into a physical patch-table or compaction contract.

### US-035 Evidence Boundary

| Boundary | Recorded result |
| --- | --- |
| Source identity | Commit `af1909c7dd248547ab9463957abb1abc72ddbe49`; Ralph's pre-existing `tasks/prd.json` modification was the only worktree change before US-035 and remains untouched. |
| Prerequisite | US-034 is complete. Its project/configuration writers and `BGO-0030`-`BGO-0039` remain the upstream mutation boundary; US-035 begins at their outbox/delta/dirty/rebuild consequences. |
| Allowed evidence | Exact production symbols and SQL, startup/role/heartbeat registration, literal non-test call closure, existing DBO identities, exact adjacent tests, and isolated disposable Bun test processes. |
| Prohibited evidence | No live/current DuckDB, approved snapshot, server, maintenance heartbeat, worker, projector, rebuild, delta intake, repair, cleanup, migration, browser, desktop shell, or product-data mutation ran. No benchmark-critical value was supplied or inferred from a resolver default. |
| State and disposition | New rows use only the US-001 `auditStatus` vocabulary. `proofCheckState`, `recommendationActionability`, and `overallCertification` remain independent; no `DSP-####`, proof state, target shape, implementation slice, recommendation, or storage disposition changed. |

### Projection And Publication Identity Boundaries

| Contract | Source-observed identity and state | Publication consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source outbox and high water | Outbox ID, source table/partition/row/operation, source high-water, idempotency key, recovery payload, retry/status | A valid recovery helper and a projector barrier do not prove an operating producer, drainer, lease claimant, or scheduler. |
| Dirty projection | Stable hash of `{projectionComponent,projectId}`; scope/article/prompt plus source partition/high-water live on mutable dirty rows/claims | New config, definition, base generation, or watermark can reuse one dirty identity; claim completion is not component publication. |
| Projection manifest | Project, component, projection identity plus mutable definition/config/generation/input/patch watermark/status | Updating a manifest under a stable key does not make its configuration or input snapshot immutable. |
| Rebuild request and chunk | Request/candidate snapshot identity plus component, article range, generation, workload, lease, retry, status and prerequisite order | Admission and chunk completion are separate from request finalization, candidate promotion, old-snapshot retirement, and deployed restart recovery. |
| Physical project scope | Project/article row in `DBO-0211`, derived from selected route/current link union direct membership and bounded by project dates | Downstream selected/display rows read physical scope. An incremental scope manifest/ack/watermark advance without a `DBO-0211` write can publish control state over stale scope. |
| Selected-import snapshot/base | Snapshot hash of definition/project/project-scope/source high water; base keyed by project/snapshot/article/list mode with winner/source fields | A `completed` header does not freeze base rows: the dirty projector later rewrites them under the same snapshot and mutates final serving. |
| Display publication | Project/snapshot/list-mode/article final-serving row plus component identities, base generation and patch watermarks | Base and patch both write `DBO-0140` directly. No separate base/patch physical lifecycle exists from which compaction or patch-row counts can be inferred. |
| Projector watermark | Project/component/projector/source partition plus high water in `DBO-0111`; advance guarded by outbox barrier and in-process lock | The barrier prevents known nonterminal outbox advance, but an in-process map does not prove cross-process uniqueness for an unkeyed persisted watermark shape. |

### US-035 Pipeline Reconciliation

- The production startup closure reaches the maintenance heartbeat and worker,
  and the worker reaches both delta-intake functions plus dirty projector
  orchestration. It does not reach `reconcileReviewServingDeltaOutboxRow`.
- Projector cycle order is rebuild recovery/execution before delta intake,
  dirty wake, and cleanup. A prioritized or failed rebuild can block all three
  later phases for that cycle.
- Review-change intake can reconcile an article delta after a current physical
  scope lookup produces no project. Import intake can reconcile rows whose
  derived project is null. Neither result proves future fan-out repair.
- Project-scope incremental acknowledgement and project-scope physical
  materialization are not the same path. Only rebuild chunk SQL materializes
  `mart.project_scope_article` membership; the startup probe merely updates and
  restores one timestamp. Selected import and display read that table.
- Selected-import base completion, later dirty mutation, final-serving refresh,
  compaction budget, and snapshot immutability are separate contracts. The
  present budget/reset helpers establish no operating compaction path.
- Display base and display patch both publish directly to the final serving
  table. The patch result's zero count conflicts with its dirty-row diagnostics
  as an operator/accounting signal, but no intended replacement value is
  inferred.
- The shared writer atomically couples configured statements/records,
  manifests, acknowledgements and watermark advance, but its in-process lock
  does not establish cross-process uniqueness for persisted watermarks, and
  mutable manifest keys do not establish immutable input snapshots.

Twelve `BGO-####` rows were added. Existing `BGO-0001`-`BGO-0039` retain their

`traced-to-writer`, while scheduler `BGO-0044` is `traced-to-lifecycle`. No API,
UI, map, DBO, CMF, FAN, PRF, DSP, TGT, or SLC row was added, removed, or

## Recommendation Proof Gate

Create separate `PRF-####` rows for positive and negative proof. For a move,
derive, archive, or delete recommendation, the minimum domains are:

| Domain | Required proof |
| --- | --- |
| API and UI/runtime | Every mounted and shared browser/desktop behavior is preserved, replaced, or proven unrelated. |
| Writer | Every direct, generated, registry-driven, or script writer and invalidation input is traced. |
| Lifecycle | Create, update, publish, pin, retire, orphan, and cleanup behavior is traced. |
| Recovery | Replay, restart, repair, startup probe, audit-history, and disaster-recovery roles are preserved or proven absent. |
| Export | Project export, PDF/bulk hydration, and other exports are preserved or proven unrelated. |
| Transfer | Transfer-package write/read mappings and compatibility needs are preserved or proven unrelated. |
| Retention | Active, failed, last-known-good, pinned, historical, and terminal retention is explicit. |
| Snapshot consistency | Identity, cursor, ordering, count, freshness, and pin semantics remain exact. |
| Benchmark and parity | Same-fixture semantics and budgets pass without retry, fallback, spill, or settings changes. |
| Migration/backfill | Replacement ownership, bounded cutover/backfill, rollback/recovery, and cleanup are explicit. |
| Bounded reads | No foreground path regresses to a project-scale scan or unbounded hydration. |

Any applicable `pending` proof keeps
`recommendationActionability: unresolved`; any applicable `blocked` proof
sets it to `blocked`. Search absence, a test-only guard, historical migration,
or baseline size alone cannot strengthen a recommendation.

## Reconciliation Summaries

For every manifest family `F`, calculate:

```text
discovered_F = count(all manifest rows in F)
classified_F = count(rows where auditStatus = classified)
out_of_scope_F = count(rows where auditStatus = out-of-scope)
blocked_F = count(rows where auditStatus = blocked)
nonterminal_F = discovered_F - classified_F - out_of_scope_F - blocked_F
required balance: discovered_F = classified_F + out_of_scope_F + blocked_F
```

The required balance is true only when `nonterminal_F = 0`. A balanced family
with `blocked_F > 0` is reconciled for accounting but still prevents
`overallCertification: PASS`. Indexes and payload/file shapes are typed
subsets of the `DBO-####` manifest and require separate summary rows.

## Inherited Status (Provisional)

This was the first durable audit artifact. It records repo-derived evidence from
the mounted API/read-contract inventory, DuckDB migrations, projector/reader
code, tests, and operator scripts. It does not inspect the live DuckDB file
directly.

The inherited version described its schema-shape recommendations as actionable
from code and schema. US-001 supersedes that disposition: its observations are
preserved, but every recommendation is provisional and
`recommendationActionability: unresolved` until revised proof is normalized.
Runtime row counts, physical bytes, null ratios, and oldest/newest update
timestamps also remain missing until collected through approved snapshot
tooling.

## Inherited API Surface Inventory

Mounted review read surfaces:

- `POST /api/articlesreviews`: LLM review rows, count state, prompt badges,
  postings, list judgment hydration, token-prefix search, async substring
  search.
- `POST /api/articlesreviewscount`: LLM count with filters and search state.
- `POST /api/articlesreviewshuman`: human review rows/count, postings,
  judgment hydration, search.
- `POST /api/articlesreviewsboth`: both-mode rows/count, LLM and human judgment
  hydration, postings, search.
- `POST /api/articlesreviewsunassessed`: unassessed queue rows/count, postings,
  queue access, search.
- `GET /api/articlesreviewsfilters`: review filter options, facets, and search
  scope.
- `GET /api/articlesreviewshumanfilters`: human filter options, facets, and
  search scope.
- `POST /api/projectsreview`: detail row, detail payload, LLM judgments, human
  judgments, prompt badges.
- `POST /api/projectsreviewswarnings`: snapshot and indexing warning state.
- `POST /api/projectsreviewshealth`: health snapshot.
- `GET /api/projects/:id/prompts/:promptId/preview`: prompt preview plus detail
  payload.
- `POST /api/articles/pdf-fetch-by-filter`: bulk/PDF selection by filter.
- `POST /api/projects/add_articles_by_filter`: bulk add by filter.
- `POST /api/articles/pdf-fetch-by-project`: PDF selection by project.
- `POST /api/articles/pdf-fetch-bulk`: PDF selection by explicit IDs.
- `POST /api/projects/:id/export`: export selection and detail hydration.

Known unmounted/internal route surface:

- `POST /api/review-serving/filter-postings`: classified in read contracts but
  not mounted; use as contract documentation only.

Parity gates already named by the repo:

- Review routes: semantic fixture, sampled parity, cursor, freshness state,
  named count state, SQL shape, forbidden foreground DuckDB work, latency, and
  response size.
- Job routes: durable job persistence, keyset batching, article-ID caps, filter
  signature, snapshot semantics, and foreground payload cap.

## Inherited Current Read Shape

The serving design already has a useful split:

- Candidate/list rows: `mart.review_article_serving_v4`.
- Filter postings: `mart.review_article_filter_posting_serving_v4`.
- Posting cardinality/statistics: `mart.review_filter_posting_stats_v4`.
- Large article payload: `mart.review_article_serving_payload_v4`.
- Judgment detail payload: `mart.review_article_judgment_detail_serving_v4`.
- Exact counts/facets/options: `mart.review_article_count_serving_v4`,
  `mart.review_filter_facet_serving_v4`, and
  `mart.review_filter_option_serving_v4`.
- Queue rows: `mart.review_unassessed_queue_serving_v4`.
- Title token-prefix search: `mart.review_title_search_serving_v4`.
- Snapshot publication/control: `app.review_serving_snapshot_manifest`,
  `app.review_projection_identity_manifest`, pins, dirty work, rebuild requests,
  and chunk manifests.

The main shape problem is not that the whole design is wrong. The problem is
that several hot rows still carry values that are only needed after candidate
selection, and some control/partial tables need explicit disposition and
retention proof.

## Inherited Schema Census

### Source, Delta, And Intake Tables

- `app.import_run_article_delta`
  - Columns: delta identity, source table/row/operation, source partition/high
    water mark, import route, article, selected rank, publication year,
    tombstone, payload JSON, reconciliation timestamps.
  - Classification: read-write delta ledger.
  - Disposition: keep.
  - Reason: import-route changes feed selected-import and project-scope
    projection.
  - Missing evidence: retention horizon and physical row count.

- `app.review_change_delta`
  - Columns: delta identity, source metadata, project/article/prompt/model,
    content flags, judgment IDs, config field set, tombstone, payload JSON.
  - Classification: read-write delta ledger.
  - Disposition: keep.
  - Reason: judgment, human judgment, prompt/config, and article changes feed
    dirty work and rebuild invalidation.
  - Missing evidence: retention horizon and payload JSON size by change kind.

- `app.review_source_change_outbox`
  - Classification: recovery outbox.
  - Disposition: keep with bounded retention.
  - Reason: preserves source-change evidence for reconciliation and recovery.
  - Missing evidence: oldest unreconciled rows and retry/quarantine aging.

- `app.review_delta_reconciliation_cursor`
  - Classification: reconciliation cursor.
  - Disposition: keep.
  - Reason: prevents replay gaps/duplicates per source partition.

- `app.review_import_article_hot_field`
  - Columns include selected rank, publication year, title, journal, external
    ID, duplicate/conflict flags, and filter bucket fields.
  - Classification: reusable hot import fact.
  - Disposition: keep, but audit `article_title`, `journal_title`, and
    `external_id` as possible display duplication.
  - Reason: selected-import and posting projectors need rank/filter facts before
    list rows are built.

### Manifest, Snapshot, And Control Tables

- `app.review_serving_dirty_work`
  - Classification: control queue.
  - Disposition: keep with retention cleanup for completed/stale rows.

- `app.review_serving_dirty_work_ack`

- `app.review_project_import_delta_cursor`

  - Proof needed: confirm no import-delta intake path reads/writes it in
    production and no operator recovery depends on it.

- `app.review_serving_projector_watermark`

- `app.review_projection_identity_manifest`

- `app.review_rebuild_request`

- `app.review_rebuild_chunk_manifest`

- `app.review_selected_import_snapshot`

- `app.review_selected_article_import_v4`

- `app.review_serving_snapshot_manifest`

- `app.review_bulk_operation_job`

### Serving And Projection Tables

- `mart.review_title_search_serving_v4`

  - Classification: hot candidate/list mart.

    semantics, publication year/date fields used for filters/order,
    duplicate/conflict flags, LLM/human status keys, prompt counts, review-open

    `url`, `full_text_pdf`, `full_text_fetched_at`,
    `full_text_conversion_status` unless a route proves pre-limit use.

    bounded.

- `mart.review_article_filter_posting_patch_v4`
  - Classification: posting patch/staging.
  - Disposition: keep until posting rebuild/incremental ownership is simplified.

- `mart.review_article_filter_posting_serving_v4`
  - Classification: hot posting index.
  - Disposition: keep and benchmark selective filter kinds.
  - Reason: prompt answer, import route, publication year, duplicate/conflict,

- `mart.review_filter_posting_stats_v4`
  - Classification: posting cardinality/statistics.
  - Disposition: keep table, keep index dropped.
  - Reason: table is still used by projector/diagnostics; migration 0114 removed
    the lookup index after it became more write cost than read benefit.

- `mart.review_article_serving_payload_v4`
  - Classification: keyed article payload.
  - Disposition: keep and expand as the home for display/detail fields that can

  - Reason: it already holds `source_metadata`, `abstract_text`,
    `full_text_preview`, and payload byte tracking by article/snapshot.

- `mart.review_article_judgment_detail_serving_v4`
  - Classification: keyed judgment payload/detail rows.
  - Disposition: keep, but split list-badge/minimal judgment fields from large

- `mart.review_article_summary_contribution_v4`
  - Classification: likely retired main summary contribution ledger.

  - Proof needed: migration removes the table; schema/static guards pass; summary

- `mart.review_article_count_serving_v4`

- `mart.review_filter_facet_serving_v4`

- `mart.review_filter_option_serving_v4`
  - Classification: filter option serving table.

  - Classification: queue serving table.
  - Disposition: keep.

  - Classification: request-scoped summary rebuild partial.
